clue.text: A copper's opening message can be charged

indicators.note: the copper's letters are opening up the message word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a cable is a telegraphed message
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A policeman's first message to a suspect could lead to charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' reads as a beginning, but here the copper's letters are opening up the message, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accusable is liable to accusation, so a charge can be brought against them.

clue.text: Not all of Camberwell Green's superior!

indicators.note: only part of the word Camberwell is used, its letters running on inside it

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a south London district's park being the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Camberwell Green is a place in south London. On traffic lights the amber lamp sits directly above the green one.
explanation.definitionFit: On a British traffic light the amber lamp is positioned just above the green, so it is literally its superior.

clue.text: Difficult case (section), ending in operation?

indicators.note: the letters of case are made difficult, that is put into disorder

parts.note: an area is a section or zone

indicators.note: the last letter of the word operation is wanted

explanation.surface: A hard childbirth case requiring a cut ends up in the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' gives CAES. Read whole, the clue describes a hard birth that ends in surgery, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesarean section is the surgical delivery used when a birth is difficult.

clue.text: Brahms (and Liszt) -Requiem, as very small part of it?

indicators.note: rhyming slang for drunk, so the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken performance of a Romantic composer's Requiem, with a tiny piece of it singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is British rhyming slang for 'pissed', i.e. drunk, so it signals an anagram of REQUIEM, AS and V. The dash is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a very short note, a tiny component of a musical work such as a requiem.

clue.text: Men cutting tree through its exterior find this animal on the surface

indicators.note: the men cut into the other letters, sitting inside them
the tree goes right through its bark, sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: bark is a tree's outer covering
the ash is a tree
kings are chessmen

explanation.surface: Soldiers felling a tree discover a creature at the water's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts ASH inside BARK to make BASHARK; 'cutting' then splits that after BAS with KINGS. Men as chessmen is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The basking shark is so named because it feeds slowly at the sea surface, as if sunbathing.

clue.text: Scalped brave unlikely to catch a thing?

indicators.note: scalping removes the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: fearless means brave

explanation.surface: A Native American warrior who has lost his scalp is unlikely to hear anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scalped' takes the head letter F off FEARLESS. Catching here means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Without ears a creature would hear nothing, being unable to catch any sound.

clue.text: Lifted by the third power cut

definitions.meaning: raised to the power three in arithmetic

explanation.surface: Something hoisted by a third authority, then reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising to the third power is cubing a number, and food cut into cubes is cubed.

clue.text: Punish murderer soundly

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: Give a killer a thorough beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' in the surface, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cane is to punish by beating with a stick.

clue.text: Holiday snap

explanation.definitionFit: A short holiday is a break, and to snap something is to break it.

clue.text: Such a grid's pointed to mad, mad cruciverbalist, ultimately: man of farce

indicators.note: the second mad says the letters before it go crazy
only the final letter of cruciverbalist is taken

parts.note: Brian Rix was a British actor famous for Whitehall farces

explanation.surface: A grid is pointed out to a crazed puzzle setter who is also a farceur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' (the second) rearranges TO and MAD into DOTMA. Brian Rix was a well-known British actor-manager of stage farces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot matrix is a rectangular grid of points used to form characters in printing or displays.

clue.text: Swimmer in mottled 1 down

indicators.note: a mottled thing is blotched and mixed up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the answer to 1 down is the colour amber

explanation.surface: Something swimming in speckled yellow-brown.
explanation.definitionFit: A bream is a freshwater fish, and a fish is a crossword swimmer.

clue.text: Demanding to be driven round Hertfordshire town

indicators.note: the word for driven goes round the town

parts.note: sent, as in driven or conveyed
Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: Someone insists on being chauffeured around a Home Counties town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent and demanding both describe strict, exacting requirements.

clue.text: Again got to study about many sheets?

indicators.note: the study word goes about the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Bought back after poring over a big pile of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the containment signal, not the abbreviation C; 'many' supplies C as the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To reacquire something is to get it again after losing it.

clue.text: Fine drizzle not popular for vegetable

parts.note: OK means fine or acceptable

indicators.note: in means popular, so those letters come out

parts.note: rain, a word for light wet weather

explanation.surface: Light showers spoil a crop that is not well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: IN meaning popular ('in fashion') is the letters 'not popular' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a green pod eaten as a vegetable, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Besides the previous filling, might this prevent another?

parts.note: too means besides or as well

indicators.note: the previous word fills the middle of the

parts.note: taken as written
past means previous

explanation.surface: A question about whether something besides an old dental filling might stop you needing a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts PAST into THE, giving THPASTE. 'filling' and 'another' play on dental fillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothpaste is used to keep teeth clean, so it may help avoid another dental filling.

clue.text: Novel report, the whole thing

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
a bang is a loud report, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: Telling a new story covers everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal but is the title SHE, H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the whole shebang' means everything, the entire affair.

clue.text: Placed before an individual state, becomes evil

parts.note: sat, as in seated or set down
taken as written
I as a single one, the Roman numeral for one
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Something put in front of a lone nation turns wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanical describes something devilish, like the Devil himself, hence wicked.

clue.text: Carol carrying little money, not hard for her to be a parasite

indicators.note: the song word holds the money letter inside it

parts.note: a carol is a song
p for penny, a small coin

indicators.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils, so it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol, with hardly any cash, lives off others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off others without giving anything back, much like a parasite.

clue.text: Is one reserved for the late programme scheduler?

definitions.text: Is one reserved for the late programme scheduler?

parts.words: Is one reserved for the late programme scheduler?
parts.note: read as a burial place reserved for the dead (the late), but it is a broadcasting term for a period scheduled late at night

explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters use this term for a late-night time period when few people watch, and it sounds like a plot for the deceased.

clue.text: This touching part of 'The Ring' explosive, encapsulating endless composition of Wagner

indicators.note: the explosive surrounds the other letters

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene

indicators.note: the remaining letters are composed afresh into a new order
the word Wagner loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tense passage of Wagner's Ring cycle, as if packed with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulating' places ANGE (from 'endless' and 'composition of' on Wagner) after the first T. 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's opera cycle but is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a line that touches a circle at just one point.

clue.text: Virtually all old masters turned up, including Turner's 'Last Ship'

indicators.note: the reversed letters take in the extra letter
in a down clue, the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: emeriti are retired professors, masters of old

indicators.note: the last letter of Turner is taken

explanation.surface: Most Old Master paintings reappear, including a Turner of a final ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virtually all' cuts EMERITI to EMERIT; 'turned up' reverses it to TIREME; R goes in after T. Old Masters looks like paintings, and Turner like the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme is an ancient galley with three banks of oars, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Boats stick to foreign water and cross

parts.note: a bat is a stick used in sport
eau is French for water
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: Vessels hold fast in strange waters and go over.
explanation.definitionFit: Bateaux is French for boats, used in English for light river craft.

clue.text: Pesticide's for this plant

parts.note: split the plant's name into two words: a pesticide is meant to cause the removal of insects

explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly plant of the borage family, and as two words it describes what a pesticide aims at.

clue.text: Smart to listen to Holy Spirit?

definitions.meaning: heard as wholly spirit, a drink with nothing added

explanation.surface: Wondering whether it is clever to heed the Holy Ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: Holy Spirit heard aloud is 'wholly spirit', alcohol with no mixer, which is how a drink served neat comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy and smart, and a neat drink is spirit taken without water or mixer.

clue.text: The Beatles' was White, though somewhat less than white

indicators.note: a little is taken off the end of the word

parts.note: albumen is the white of an egg

explanation.surface: A remark that the Beatles' record was white, or rather a bit less than white.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles' 1968 double record is known as the White Album.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' self-titled 1968 record is popularly called the White Album.

clue.text: Gap widens, right around the extent of rail, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A gap gets wider on the right of a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like a railway track but is the bird of that name, so the definition is the span of its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Wingspread is the distance across a bird's outstretched wings, and the rail is a marsh bird.

clue.text: Capital of Denmark, alias that of Russia and that of Senegal

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one, of Denmark

parts.note: aka stands for also known as, an alias

indicators.note: that refers back to capital, so the first letter of Russia is wanted

explanation.surface: A list of European capitals, and that of an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city but means first letter, until the last 'that of', where it really is the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dakar is the capital city of Senegal in West Africa.

clue.text: See 16
Spanish gentleman hired vehicle to go across the Pyrenees, coming to nothing

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle for hire
aller is French for to go, France lying across the Pyrenees from Spain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Spanish gent takes a taxi over the mountains, but gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the Pyrenees' means in France, seen from Spain, so 'to go' is French ALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is Spanish for a gentleman or knight, literally a horseman.

clue.text: See 4
Not entirely relaxed, it proving extreme

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: limp means relaxed or slack

explanation.surface: Being only partly at ease shows how far things can go.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the extreme point beyond which one cannot go.

clue.text: He has to drop aitches to offer — himself?

indicators.note: the letter H is removed from each word, as in a Cockney accent

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
taken as written before the deletion
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A man who must drop his H sounds offers himself up.
explanation.walkthrough: An East Ender is a Londoner from the East End, whose Cockney accent famously drops the H sound, saying 'e 'as.
explanation.definitionFit: The man who drops his aitches is a Cockney Londoner from the East End, so the clue describes himself.
